subject: AegisCore upgrade: sudden p95 latency and 5xx spike after v4.1/q4_0
messages:
From: Alexandra Vega <avega@aegiscore.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-alerts@aegiscore.com, Raj Patel <rpatel@aegiscore.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: sudden latency + 5xx after v4.1/q4_0 deploy (urgent)

Hi Olga,

We just flipped to Redwood model v4.1 with the q4_0 quant profile at 08:30 UTC and immediately saw our p95 jump from ~220ms to ~980ms and a spike in 5xx errors (approx 6% of requests) against our production inference endpoints. This is customer-impacting — checkout the attached logs for 08:30-09:05 UTC.

Can you confirm whether this profile change was expected to increase CPU scheduling or inference latency? We need a rollback plan and an ETA. Our SLAs are tight; customers are seeing failed responses in checkout flows.

Thanks,
Alexandra Vega
Head of Platform Reliability
AegisCore

Attachments: aegiscore_5xx_logs_20280524.txt, p95_traces_pod-12.csv
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Vega <avega@aegiscore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:28:15 -0000
Subject: Re: sudden latency + 5xx after v4.1/q4_0 deploy (urgent)

Alexandra — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. I'm pulling the infra and runtime leads in this thread.

Preliminary notes: v4.1/q4_0 was expected to slightly increase CPU utilization but not p95 by this magnitude. Possible causes:kernel selection mismatch for q4_0 on that GPU generation, or an unintended fallback path hitting synchronous decode.

Immediate next steps I'm proposing:
- Irene/Runtime: confirm whether kernel selection for q4_0 changed at deploy time and whether we saw any OOM/GPUD-side throttles.
- Dylan/Infra: look at autoscaler and pod churn 08:25–09:00 UTC; are requests being funneled to a small subset?
- I'll open a canary rollback and hold any further profile flips until we agree.

Marissa — flagging for CS and credits discussion if this becomes an SLA event.

Olga
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Alexandra Vega <avega@aegiscore.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 09:41:32 -0000
Subject: Re: sudden latency + 5xx after v4.1/q4_0 deploy (urgent)

On Wed, May 24, 2028 at 09:28 Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Preliminary notes: v4.1/q4_0 was expected to slightly increase CPU utilization but not p95 by this magnitude.

Checked the kernel logs and AMX selection telemetry. There was an unexpected fallback to a compatibility kernel on the affected 12-GPU pool around 08:29:10 UTC — likely due to a tight workspace allocation triggered by the new quantized KV cache layout. When that fallback occurs we see longer synchronous loops and higher tail latency. No OOMs recorded but decode latencies per token doubled in those traces.

I recommend an immediate rollback of the q profile for production and a canary deploy of v4.1 with q2_0 on a 10% traffic slice while we debug kernel selection heuristics. I'll prepare a short postmortem and include the kernel trace.

Irene
Runtime Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alexandra Vega <avega@aegiscore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 10:03:57 -0000
Subject: Re: sudden latency + 5xx after v4.1/q4_0 deploy (urgent)

Alexandra — infra update: we observed pod rotation on the aegiscore-prod-12 pool starting 08:27 UTC (autoscaler reacted to short-lived CPU spikes) which concentrated requests onto 2 hot pods by 08:29 UTC. Those pods ran the compatibility kernel Irene mentions. We're forcing traffic redistribution and temporarily scaling the pool + triggering a warm-up of additional nodes.

Action taken:
- scaled aegiscore-prod-12 from 12->20 nodes (in flight)
- started a controlled rollback plan: will flip q4_0->q2_0 on the oldest model flavor at 10:15 UTC unless AegisCore requests immediate rollback now.

Marcus — please prep the rollback runbook and the canary gating checks.

Dylan
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 10:20:05 -0000
Subject: Exec heads-up: AegisCore production degradation (p95 latency, 5xx spike)

Marissa — flagging this as an SLA-impacting incident for one of our top enterprise customers. Irene and Dylan have identified a compatibility-kernel fallback tied to q4_0 and autoscaler concentration. We have a rollback plan scheduled for 10:15 UTC to q2_0 canary, then full rollback if gating fails.

If canary fails we'll need: a) an SLA credit recommendation, b) a brief exec summary for AegisCore leadership (they've looped their Head of Platform), and c) a postmortem commitment timeline.

I'll keep you posted; please escalate to CS leadership if needed.

Olga
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dave Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 May 2028 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Exec heads-up: AegisCore production degradation (p95 latency, 5xx spike)

Thanks for the updates and quick actions everyone. Canary rollback to q2_0 completed at 10:41 UTC on 24 May and we observed the p95 drop back to ~230ms and 5xx back to baseline within the canary slice. Full rollback finished by 11:05 UTC and AegisCore reports normal traffic.

Next steps for follow-up:
- Irene to own kernel-selection patch and test matrix (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Dylan Marcus to validate autoscaler sensitivity and heat distribution (ETA: 1 week).
- CS: provide AegisCore a one-time credit for the window of impact (Olga/Marissa to propose).
- Postmortem draft due by 2028-06-07; include mitigations and a retrospective call with AegisCore.

Alexandra/AegisCore — thank you for the quick signal and patience. We'll share the postmortem and proposed credit by next week.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
